By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 15:49, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 15:54.

Now down to third in the Serie A standings, Scudetto holders Inter Milan will try to give their title defence a boost when Genoa visit San Siro on Saturday night.

Recent results have seen Inter slip behind both Rome clubs, but they gained a vital European victory in midweek; meanwhile, their visitors have surged into the top half after recovering from a rocky start.

Having exited at the first knockout round last season, Inter started this term's Champions League campaign by taking nothing from their first two fixtures - but​ things have improved dramatically since then.

Three straight wins without conceding have moved them up the table, and Cristian Chivu's side now occupy a playoff place - in fact, finishing inside the top eight cannot be ruled out.

After defeating Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord, the Nerazzurri beat Stuttgart 2-0 on Wednesday night, as captain Lautaro Martinez scored his first goal since returning from injury.

That partly made amends for throwing away two Serie A points three days beforehand, when Inter played out a chaotic 4-4 draw with local rivals Atalanta BC.

Despite Pio Esposito's first top-flight hat-trick, they let in a couple of avoidable late goals that left them three points behind surprise leaders Lazio, with Roma sandwiched between.

Now, the Nerazzurri will aim to put pressure on both capital clubs by posting a customary home win over Genoa.

Such has been their dominance, Inter have won all of the last 12 league meetings at San Siro, keeping 10 clean sheets and only conceding two goals.

Either home or away, Genoa have won none of their last 14 clashes with Inter, so they may be dreading an upcoming double-header.

Just days after this league game, the Grifone must return to Milan for a cup tie, as the sides vie for a place in the Coppa Italia quarter-finals.

Though their past record makes for grim reading, present form suggests Genoa can at least give the Italian champions a scare, as they have won five of their last seven Serie A matches.

Since Daniele De Rossi swerved the sack during the October international break, his rejuvenated side have shot up the table, swapping the drop zone for the top half.

Last weekend, the Rossoblu beat lowly Sassuolo 2-0 thanks to a Milutin Osmajic brace, posting back-to-back away wins for the first time since 2024.

Some 12 years have passed since Genoa recorded three successive away wins at Italy's elite level, and few would expect them to do so on Saturday.

Inter Milan form (all competitions):.

Inter will be missing set-piece specialist Hakan Calhanoglu and back-up striker Ange Bonny due to thigh injuries, while Piotr Zielinski and Alessandro Bastoni are both doubts.

Bastoni was substituted before half time against Stuttgart, and it remains to be seen if he will recover from a muscular problem in time to play.

After scoring as a substitute in midweek, Martinez must vie with Marcus Thuram and in-form Esposito to feature up front.

Level with the latter pair in the Capocannoniere race, Genoa striker Osmajic has scored six goals in his first 12 Serie A appearances. The Montenegrin is almost certain to start, as fellow forward Lorenzo Colombo suffered an ACL injury last weekend, probably curtailing his 2026-27 campaign.

Leo Ostigard was recently hospitalised with a high fever, but he is still expected to lead the visitors' three-man defence in Milan.

Key midfielder Morten Frendrup has been struggling with an ankle problem, meaning he faces a race against time.

Inter Milan possible starting lineup:.

It has been revealed that J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Augusto; Spence, Barella, Sucic, Jones, Dimarco; Esposito, L. Martinez.

Genoa possible starting lineup:.

Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ehizibue, Frendrup, Traore, Ellertsson; Messias, El Shaarawy; Osmajic.

Not only are they traditionally dominant in this fixture, but Inter have also won all of their last six Serie A home games while scoring at least twice.

Though they sometimes start slowly - and Genoa have scored a remarkable 77% of their league goals during the first half - the Nerazzurri will not be stopped.

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.

This young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Liverpool came from two goals behind, and it all ended with a panic that meant they came close to chucking it away again. But what everyone could agree on from this strange match of fluctuating fortunes was that Ngumoha looks like one of the best young players in Europe. He is also a bona fide two-sided winger, winning this game for Liverpool from the right wing rather than his conventional left-wing role.

Recent findings suggest that ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment. That was an electrifying run into a group of converging yellow shirts in which he beat two men and still retained the composure to pick out Mac Allister in the area. Even as the Argentine ran to the Kop to celebrate, that stand was chanting the name of the teenager from east London. Ngumoha was one of three academy boys in Andoni Iraola’s XI, along with Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni, and all had an impact.

From an attacking point of view, Iraola agreed, Ngumoha had periods of the game when he looked unstoppable. “If we can put Rio in situations one-v-one, he makes plays, [and] he produces things,” Iraola stated. “The assist for Alexis is a lovely play. He could go down for a penalty but he decides to continue which is a great decision. Also endurance-wise he is able to play more minutes.”.

Industry observers note that he becomes the youngest Liverpool player in Champions League history to register an assist in the competition. For Iraola it will be hard to leave Ngumoha out of the game against in-form Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday. “I believe in myself to do it,” Ngumoha mentioned to Amazon Prime TV. “The more chances we get, the more it makes the opposition worry. I just keep going and be ruthless.”.

It has been revealed that iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. In a recent development, “They are so good on the ball,” Iraola noted of Villarreal afterwards. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

Subs: Junior, Costa, Freeman, Diatta, Gerard, Foyth, Akhomach, Macia, Oluwaseyi, Perez, El Jmili, Gaitan Diaz.

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Gravenberch, Nyoni, Mac Allister; Ngumoha, Koumas, Gakpo.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Kerkez, Wirtz, Isak, Barcola, Chambers, McConnell, Danns, Laffey.

A very interesting team selection from Andoni Iraola. Liverpool’s head coach had indicated at his pre-match press conference that he was going to go as strong as possible, as his side seek to secure their third straight Champions League win. But the very fact Iraola has chosen to put Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola on the bench indicates he has one eye on Sunday’s demanding assignment against Brighton at Anfield.

Sources indicate that iraola will be delighted to have Cody Gakpo fit again and Lewis Koumas certainly deserves another opportunity to lead the line. But after victory’s against Atletico Madrid and LASK, Liverpool have given themselves some breathing space and it is understandable if Iraola, who has bemoaned the lack of time he has to train his squad, is already plotting Brighton’s downfall.

Your Reds to take on Villarreal in the #UCL! 🔴💫 https://t.co/tlQNFZVMBv.

According to recent reports, the club known as the “Yellow Submarine” made themselves some fans in the red half of Merseyside by denying Everton a place in the Champions League proper in 2005/06. Everton lost 4-2 on aggregate, and there was controversy in the second leg in Spain when Pierluigi Collina disallowed a Duncan Ferguson header that could have taken the tie to extra time. Everton had finished fourth, one place above Liverpool, the previous season, but Liverpool’s triumph in Istanbul assured them of a qualification place too. Unlike Everton, they prevailed.

Speaking of which, Rafael Benitez is at Anfield this evening.

Sources indicate that dominic King takes stock of Andoni Iraola’s first 10 games in charge of Liverpool and, despite some teething problems, he believes there are reasons to be optimistic. The demands Iraola is putting on Liverpool’s midfielders are an interesting tactical wrinkle, with Dom writing: “Liverpool’s formation will always be written as 4-2-3-1, but the reality is that Iraola’s team do not play in four clear tactical lines. He asks specific jobs of his midfielders, deploying them detailed instructions, and it is going to require some patience before performances become consistent.”.

A precious victory at Brentford, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak among the goals and a couple of improved showings from Florian Wirtz mean things now look a little brighter for Liverpool.

They are strong favourites to make it nine points from nine in the Champions League by beating Villarreal at Anfield this evening, the Spanish club they vanquished in the 2022 semi-finals under Jürgen Klopp.

Liverpool drew Atletico Madrid at home (already ticked off) and Inter Milan away as their two pot-one fixtures, which is about as kind as you can expect. A top-two finish in the league phase is a realistic aspiration for Andoni Iraola’s team, and something would need to go badly awry for them to miss out on the top eight.

Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Isak returned from injury to strengthen Liverpool at Brentford, although Szoboszlai has been lost for a few weeks following another hamstring complication.

Villarreal have punched well above their weight in Europe for the past few decades, reaching two European Cup semi-finals (beaten by Arsenal in 2006 as well as Liverpool in 2022) and winning the Europa League under Unai Emery in 2021.

In a recent development, they have been mediocre in La Liga so far this season though, 12th after nine games on nine points and with a goal difference of zero. Their Champions League performances have been promising though, losing by the odd goal in a frantic finish at Borussia Dortmund and beating Napoli 3-1 at home. Villarreal’s best player is probably Senegalese central midfielder Pape Gueye, and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pépé is also in their ranks. Gueye, despite his position, is their joint-top scorer in all competitions with three goals.

It has been revealed that iraola will be up against his close friend and former Athletic Bilbao team-mate Inigo Perez who is now in charge at Villarreal. Perez was also Iraola’s assistant at Rayo Vallecano, the job which earned the Basque his move to Bournemouth. Perez guided Rayo Vallecano to the Uefa Conference League final last season.

Rasmus Hojlund has laid bare the suffocating pressure of playing for Manchester United and given his insight into what Mauricio Pochettino’s squad will be suffering while marooned in the Premier League relegation zone.

The Dane was back in town this week after spending two seasons at United, mocking Manchester City fans when scoring the opener of Napoli’s 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night.

Hojlund secured a £38million permanent move away from Old Trafford in the summer but remains in touch with plenty of old team-mates and believes the lack of equilibrium at the club has contributed to a steady decline.

‘There are so many people following the club around the world and you can’t really escape from it,’ Hojlund said.

It has been revealed that ‘It is almost too high when it is good and almost too low when it is bad. It is all about trying to be in that middle. I had both the highs and the lows there.

It has been revealed that ‘The pressure is part of the club, it comes with playing for United. There has been a lot of change but hopefully they will get it right with Mauricio.’.

Rasmus Hojlund mocked Man City fans after scoring for Napoli at the Etihad on Tuesday night.

A United supporter, Hojlund laughed off the idea that the club is in a relegation scrap despite their worst start to a season since 1972. And the 23-year-old revealed that the players were ready for ‘change’ following the sacking of Michael Carrick.

‘I spoke with Bruno [Fernandes] and Diogo [Dalot] during the international break and they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going but also looking forward to some change,’ Hojlund added.

Sources indicate that ‘I am still speaking with Patrick [Dorgu] and I just wish the guys all the best. I am sure they will turn it around this season. They have got a lot of quality. They have got a great squad, good leaders, good professionals.

Sources indicate that ‘It is a temporary picture, I think they will get back to the top. The Premier League is like this. I read the other day that Bournemouth was in the relegation zone after a couple of games, now they have won the last five games and are in the top half of the table.’.

Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1,2,3. Portland cement manufacturing is among the most challenging industrial processes to decarbonize, yet it remains indispensable for building the infrastructure underpinning the low-carbon transition4,5. Here, building beyond the two-century-old conventional cement process6, we report a route that creates sustainable cement, by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds. Our technique generates localized temperatures up to 2,400 °C, sufficient to liquefy the raw materials. These liquid-phase reactions promote elemental mixing and solidification, producing reactive clinker phases. Our in situ transmission electron microscopy captures the early-stage cement hydration process in real time, revealing that surface disorder accelerates clinker reactivity by facilitating the dynamic nucleation and growth of hydration clusters. Beyond typical limestone and clay feedstocks, we show that hydrated cement paste from waste concrete can also be processed into clinkers, meeting ordinary Portland cement specifications. By coupling circular resource use with ultrafast electrified processing, our approach enables sustainable, low-cost cement production at scale.

It has been revealed that phase diagram of the binary system CaO–SiO2, adapted from Day and Shepherd16, illustrating the composition, possible secondary phases, and transition and melting temperatures for both C2S and C3S. In cement chemist notation: C = CaO, S = SiO2, F = Fe2O3, and A = Al2O3. Trd represents tridymite. Tricalcium silicate (3CaO·SiO2, C3S), dicalcium silicate (2CaO·SiO2, C2S), tricalcium aluminate (3CaO·Al2O3, C3A), and calcium alumino-ferrite (4CaO·Al2O3·Fe2O3, C4AF), with impurities, are commonly referred to as alite, belite, aluminate, and ferrite, respectively.

(a) Characterization of carbon fibres. SEM images of the carbon fibres used in MCP heating experiment, showing a fibre diameter of approximately 7.5 μm. (b) Chemical mapping of cement raw meal (RM) with a particle size of D50 = 4.6 μm. The primary components of the raw meal are limestone (CaCO3) and clay minerals (SiO2, Al2O3), as identified in the Ca, Si, and Al elemental maps. The milling process induces the formation of fine, intermixed aggregates, where individual particles become closely attached with each other. This intimate mixing enhances the homogeneity of the raw meal. The formation of these aggregates is particularly beneficial in facilitating efficient fusion and clinker formation, as the localized heating effect promotes uniform thermal decomposition and phase transformation within the RM particles.

In a recent development, (a) Temperature profiles of gas (purple) and raw meal (blue) in a commercial rotary kiln system compared to our method (orange). We note that temperature non-uniformity can still be significant in conventional cement kiln, with local temperature differences on the order of several hundred degrees Celsius (up to ~600 °C) between the raw meal and gas flame, which contributes to inefficient heat transfer and over-burning/under-burning risks in the clinker bed. (b) Diagram of raw meal transitioning to clinker in a conventional kiln over time. By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 15:54, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 15:56.

Malaga's search for their first victory of the 2026-27 La Liga campaign will continue on Saturday afternoon when they welcome Athletic Bilbao to Estadio La Rosaleda.

Athletic have won two of the last three meetings between the two sides and also lead the overall head-to-head record 13 victories to Malaga's 11.

Malaga have a record of zero wins, five draws and eight defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with five points leaving them bottom of the La Liga table.

There is still plenty of football to be played this season, but they are currently seven points behind 17th-placed Valencia and will not want that to be stretched to 10 points in the next gameweek.

Juan Francisco Funes' side secured a return to La Liga through the 2025-26 Segunda Division playoffs, but they have found it tough to adjust to life back at this level.

Los Albicelestes will enter this match off the back of three straight losses to Real Betis, Racing de Santander and Osasuna, but they have managed to win once this season - a 3-0 success over Alcazar in the Copa del Rey at the end of October.

Malaga held Athletic to a 3-3 draw when the pair last locked horns at La Rosaleda, while their last win over the Basque side was a 2-1 success in October 2016.

As for Athletic, a record of four wins, four draws and four defeats from 12 matches has left them eighth in the table on 16 points, three points behind sixth-placed Sevilla heading into the next gameweek.

The Lions will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 defeat to Espanyol, which proved to be their first loss since October 21 away to Levante.

Edin Terzic's side have picked up 11 points from their seven home league matches this season, while they have claimed five points from their five games on their travels.

Athletic finished 12th in Spain's top flight last season, so there is clear room for improvement during the current campaign, with a European spot certainly the target.

The Lions will take on Numancia in the Copa del Rey in their first match of December before hosting Real Madrid in their next league game on December 6.

Malaga form (all competitions):.

Athletic Bilbao form (all competitions):.

Malaga will welcome Adam Aznou back into their squad this weekend, with the 20-year-old serving a one-game suspension against Osasuna last time out.

However, Rafita, Fernardo Calero, Julen Lobete and Aaron Ochoa are again expected to be unavailable for selection due to injury problems.

Adrian Nino has scored five times in nine appearances for Malaga this season, and the 22-year-old is set to continue in the final third of the field.

As for Athletic, Unai Eguiluz, Gorka Guruzeta, Maroan Sannadi and Dani Vivian will miss the match due to injury problems.

Head coach Terzic is expected to resist the temptation to shuffle his pack for this game despite the disappointment of the defeat to Espanyol.

Inaki Williams featured through the middle last time out, with Nico Williams to the left and Alex Berenguer to the right - that is again expected to be the case in this match.

Herrero; Murillo, Pastor, Recio, Aznou; Munoz, Rodriguez, Martinez, Larrubia; Dotor, Nino.

Simon; Rincon, Alvarez, Laporte, Berchiche; Prados, Canales; Berenguer, Sancet, N Williams; I Williams.

Malaga have drawn half (three) of their home league games this season, while Athletic have just one away victory to their name, so we are backing a stalemate here.

Tech Report: Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (716 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, high intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work.
  • Across 826 people in the United States and China, women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often.
  • The study examined whether people's cognitive ability affects how their teammates treat them and whether that differs between women and men.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, high intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work. But a upcoming study suggests that for women, it can also lead to worse treatment from colleagues.

Across 826 people in the United States and China, women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often. Men with high scores did not receive such treatment, and in one group, they were treated better.

The study examined whether people's cognitive ability affects how their teammates treat them and whether that differs between women and men.

It has been revealed that since it was published this year, Nitya Chawla, an associate professor at UCL School of Management in London and the researcher behind the study, indicates women have written to her saying the findings matched their own experience at work. Some told her they had wondered whether they were to blame for hostility.

The researchers ran two studies. The first followed 432 business students at a US public university working in small teams on a consulting project for real organizations. The second surveyed 394 full-time employees working in teams at a financial manufacturer in China.

Intelligence here means cognitive ability measured with a standardized test of reasoning and problem-solving that employers use in hiring. Teammates were not told of anyone's scores. They rated one another, and a few weeks later each person reported how much help they had received and how often they had been undermined, for instance by having information withheld.

In a recent development, the effects were small, and the study shows a link, not proof that colleagues' perceptions caused the treatment. Participants reported help and mistreatment themselves, and the study did not look at race or ethnicity.

In the student group, the difference between women and men was no longer statistically significant when two participants with extremely low scores were included.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers point to social role theory, the idea that people expect men and women to fit traditional roles: men as capable and assertive, women as warm and supportive. A woman with high cognitive ability breaks that expectation, and colleagues may assume she lacks warmth.

"It's that automatic, implicit assumption that takes place alongside the presence of intelligence that then drives these more negative interpersonal behaviors," Chawla told DW.

In both groups, women with higher scores were rated as more hostile. Among the employees in China, they were also rated as less warm. Women seen as more hostile reported less help, both with their work and on a personal level, and more undermining.

The team also checked whether the women were simply behaving differently. Higher-scoring women were rated as somewhat more domineering, but that did not explain why they received less help or more mistreatment. The findings point to colleagues' assumptions, Chawla claims, rather than to anything the women did.

Industry observers note that no, men with high intelligence scores do not face the same treatment. Among the students in the United States, a man's score made no difference to how his teammates rated or treated him.

Among the employees in China, men with higher scores were rated as less hostile, received more help and were mistreated less often. The authors suggest the difference between the two groups may reflect cultural differences in gender norms, but they did not test this.

Industry observers note that no, Chawla indicates. "That would be really the wrong conclusion to draw.".

Sources indicate that small effects still matter, she argues, because they are experienced day after day. Over time, this kind of treatment can lead to anxiety, self-doubt and a sense of not belonging. "These experiences and these feelings can become very, very burdensome over time," she said.

Chawla puts the responsibility on workplaces rather than on women. Managers, she indicates, should track how team members treat one another, and organizations should hold regular check-ins to see whether employees are getting equal support.

Individuals can ask themselves a simple question, she notes: would they react the same way if that colleague were a man?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

According to recent reports, in that instance, United fans booed Solskjaer. Carrick at least received some polite applause from the fans, who are a smart bunch and know the club’s problems extend far beyond the man in the dugout. Still, it is always the manager who pays the price. Solskjaer remarked he knew at half-time he was toast and Carrick is now under real threat himself – and seemingly at loggerheads with his captain.

Fernandes’s criticism of United’s set-up and approach was cutting and a direct attack on his manager and backroom team. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” the United captain mentioned.

There may be some truth in that, but Carrick’s response felt the most accurate assessment of the lot and will certainly chime with supporters who have long questioned how and why so many United sides, regardless of the manager, reach a point where running, intensity and urgency seem optional. “Whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win,” Carrick noted.

According to recent reports, carrick has been telling us for weeks that he and his squad are together, that the team are not too far away, that it is all about small margins. He even described Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds as a “fresh start”. But Como blew the lid off any pretence of that being the case. Even by the standards of this season to date, though, what unfolded here in the rain in Lombardy was shocking to witness.

Como, inspired by the outstanding Nico Paz, were every bit as good as United – who have won just two of 11 games this season – were a pitiful mess.

Sources indicate that having conceded after just 47 seconds to Atlético Madrid last week, United were behind after only 118 seconds this time. That in itself told you a lot about these players and this team and it set the tone for what was to follow: a masterclass in incompetence and indifference. There have only been four worse results in United’s European history, although you will struggle to find a poorer performance than this.

You looked at Como and it was clear every player knew their job and role and went about it with relish. There were patterns of play, they ran, there was intensity and movement and they were quicker to everything.

According to recent reports, paz scored the first and third goals and set up a wondrous second for Tasos Douvikas that showcased Como’s talent at the same time as underlining United’s myriad fault lines. Paz was just unplayable for much of an evening when United never got close to getting to grips with the young Argentine, whose big physique belies a bewitching ability on the ball. Jacobo Ramón completed the rout before Joshua Zirkzee scored the most hollow of goals for United late on.

Sources indicate that united, by contrast, were a sorry collection of strangers. It was impossible to discern a game strategy. United were sent out in a strange 4-2-4, with Fernandes and Youri Tielemans operating as almost double false nines. Glenn Hoddle said on TNT Sports that it was like United were “playing in chains”.

Recent findings suggest that neither looked sure of what they were supposed to be doing. There was just a giant hole where the attack should have been. Everything about them was slow, leaden. The confusion was contagious. Everywhere you looked there were players second-guessing themselves, uncertain of their role and position and habitually a yard or two or three off the pace. But was there any excuse for not running, for so little effort?

Michael Carrick has insisted there is not a “toxic culture” at Manchester United in the wake of scathing criticism from former manager Erik ten Hag of the Old Trafford hierarchy and player power at the club.

The current United manager – who is under pressure after the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years – also believes he has the backing of the United board, despite Ten Hag accusing Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos regime of a series of “broken promises”.

In an interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag blamed Ratcliffe and his executives for fuelling a “toxic culture” by giving power to players and failing to back him on disciplinary matters relating to Marcus Rashford, Jadon Sancho and other first-teamers.

But Carrick noted he had not encountered any toxicity since taking over from Ruben Amorim in January and suggested United’s last two outings, a 1-1 draw against Leeds United and a 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid, underlined the camaraderie in the group.

“Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give,” Carrick said before Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Cesc Fàbregas’s Como in northern Italy, where he is battling an injury and illness crisis.

“We’ve had some good performances. We’ve had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We’ve made some mistakes.

“But I have to say, the type of performance put into the weekend and for large parts against Atlético, there’s a lot of togetherness there. There’s a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is important.”.

Andrey Santos, one of United’s summer signings, was asked for his thoughts on Lisandro Martínez’s explosive interview in which he took aim at the club’s hierarchy for their strategy in the latest transfer window. The Brazilian remarked: “We know the comments [of] Licha, but I think now it’s done so we have to move on and focus on tomorrow [Wednesday].

When pressed on whether Martínez had addressed the squad about his remarks, Santos added: “No, no, no. Nothing happened, as you know we are on the same page, so we believe in ourselves, in your team-mates, your coach, your staff, so I think this is the most important.”.

Inter Miami forward Luis Suarez has confirmed he is in talks with the MLS club over a latest contract.

Suarez is in the closing stages of his third full season with Inter Miami after signing on a free transfer at the start of 2024.

The Uruguayan has scored 59 goals in 120 competitive appearances, including 17 strikes in 30 regular-season MLS games this season.

However, as it stands, Suarez is on course to become a free agent when his current deal expires at the end of the calendar year.

In theory, Friday's must-win playoff game against Columbus Crew could be his last, although he has revealed he is in talks over a fresh deal.

"We're already in talks with the club to find the best solution for both sides," Suarez told reporters on Wednesday.

"But honestly, my focus is more on the match against Columbus this Friday than on what will happen in the future.".

Inter Miami are one down in their three-match series against Columbus after falling to a heavy 3-0 defeat at the Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Gonzalo Tapia opened the scoring with a ninth-minute penalty, before Gonzalo Lujan's 36th-minute red card forced Inter Miami to play over 50 minutes with 10 men.

Columbus took full advantage to net two second-half goals to leave Inter Miami requiring a win at the ScottsMiracle-Gro Field to force a deciding game in the first-round tie.

Suarez has made it clear that "the time for excuses is over" as the Herons look to prolong their defence of the MLS Cup.

“It’s clear we are at a club where we have an obligation to win,” Suarez remarked.

Recent findings suggest that “If we get eliminated on Friday, it will be a disappointment. We have to be that clear about it.

"The time for excuses is over...it’s time to face reality. If we are eliminated, we will be the first to be self-critical, although we hope that doesn’t happen.

Industry observers note that “I believe the squad are at a point where we understand that it’s time to deliver. This is our final opportunity.

"This format has given us another chance to play this Friday, and it’s the last shot we have to bring the series back home.”.

The visitors experienced disappointment in their last trip to Columbus in September, when they fell to a 2-1 defeat following a stoppage-time winner.

According to information from Sky Sportsthe Red Devils captain has refused a second contract extension offer, while his current commitment expires at the end of the season. The 32-year-old Portuguese attacking midfielder had already rejected a first proposal made last summer, when discussions began between the two parties. Despite these two refusals, Manchester United does not intend to abandon negotiations and still wishes to keep its captain. The English club also has an option allowing it to unilaterally extend its contract for an additional season, which would prevent Fernandes from negotiating freely with foreign teams from January for a free departure. A situation which could quickly become one of the major concerns for Mancunian leaders, while Mauricio Pochettino should be officially appointed coach this Friday to succeed Michael Carrick, dismissed on Thursday.

Recent findings suggest that already very popular in recent months, Bruno Fernandes notably refused a considerable financial offer from Al-Hilal in June. The Saudi club were ready to almost triple his weekly salary of 250,000 euros, while offering 100 million euros to Manchester United to secure his transfer. Galatasaray had also expressed their interest, but the English leaders then assured that their captain was not for sale. Voted best player of the year by English journalists in May, then by his peers in August, after a season marked by 21 assists, Fernandes, however, is experiencing a much more complicated exercise. The Portuguese has scored just four goals this season, including a hat-trick against Ipswich Town in August, in Manchester United’s only Premier League victory so far. The expected arrival of Mauricio Pochettino could now constitute an crucial element in the discussions around his future. The two men could have worked together as early as 2019, when the Argentinian coached Tottenham, but Sporting Portugal ultimately blocked the transfer of the attacking midfielder.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave newly introduced era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

According to recent reports, he mentioned: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”.

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”.

This was not as comfortable but still an impressive performance from this new and exciting team. Alysson, the Brazilian winger, was their man of the match.

Emery had warned his players of complacency against the Norwegian champions, but Villa took command from the start and were ahead after 23 minutes.

Ross Barkley scored twice against Fenerbahce last week and was in the right place again to head Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner past Arild Ostbo.

What are fossil fuels?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (605 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life.
  • The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.
  • Industry observers note that they started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life. But now they threaten to make the planet unlivable for many plants, animals and humans.

The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.

Industry observers note that they started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals. When they died, they sank to the bottom of oceans and swamps where they decomposed under layers of sediment.

According to recent reports, over time, this matter was buried deeper and deeper into the earth, subjecting it to increasing pressure and heat which changed its chemical composition. Plants and trees transformed into coal, whereas microscopic plankton and algae became oil and — if the heat and pressure increased further — gas.

Today fossil fuels can be found in the earth's crust all around the world although some countries, such as the US, Saudi Arabia and Russia, have bigger reserves than others.

Coal, found in underground coal beds, is extracted by mining, whereas oil and gas, found in reservoirs beneath the land and ocean, are accessed by drilling.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since the early 19th Century, when the discovery and exploitation of fossil fuel reserves powered the Industrial Revolution, our use of them has skyrocketed, increasing eight-fold since 1950.

Today they provide 80% of our energy needs through heating, electricity generation and transport.

In a recent development, we transform them into energy either by burning them directly in furnaces that warm up our homes and businesses, or in power plants to heat water into steam which then generates electricity. When it comes to transport, crude oil is refined into a range of products such as diesel, gasoline and kerosene that are burned in the engines of automobiles, airplanes and ships. Natural gas is also sometimes compressed for use in cars and buses.

But fossil fuels are also essential to a huge range of products including steel, formed using a coal-derived material called coke, and plastic, which is produced by refining and processing crude oil and gas.

Fossil fuels are by far the biggest contributors to climate change. When burned to power our modern lives, they emit carbon dioxide (CO2) into Earth's atmosphere, trapping heat and causing temperatures to rise.

With 2025 officially one of the warmest years on record, the impact of these emissions is being felt around the world. Hotter temperatures are causing polar ice caps to melt and creating the conditions for extreme weather events — such as floods, drought, wildfires and storms — to become more intense and frequent.

In a recent development, scientists stress the need to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) to avoid unleashing the most catastrophic impacts of climate change. That was laid out in the 2015 Paris Agreement. At the moment, there are 194 parties to the agreement, but progress has been too slow, and overall emissions continue to rise.

Three years after countries agreed at the UN climate conference in Dubai COP28 to transition away from coal, oil and gas. After the previous COP in Brazil failed to reach a consensus on a concrete blueprint, Brazil has now presented a roadmap aimed at turning that promise into national plans.

"It is long past time to stop treating the transition away from fossil fuels as taboo or intractable," United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres noted.

England manager Thomas Tuchel has been told to consider an unusual solution to Harry Kane's injury absence if the Three Lions captain misses March's Nations League quarter-final with Norway.

Tuchel and co are sweating over the fitness of the Ballon d'Or winner after he was ruled out for a 'few months' with a serious ankle injury, sustained in Bayern Munich's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln earlier this month.

Kane had to undergo surgery to correct the torn ligament, and there is a chance that he could now sit out the reunion with World Cup quarter-final foes Norway, whom the Three Lions face at the end of March 2027.

Tuchel has a plethora of alternative centre-forward options at his disposal, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Dominic Solanke, Ivan Toney, Ollie Watkins and Championship star Will Lankshear.

However, ex-England forward Brian Deane has exclusively told Sports Mole that Tuchel could instead consider using either Jude Bellingham or Morgan Rogers as a false nine rather than deploying a pure centre-forward.

“It is difficult because I do not think England have another centre-forward who can do exactly what Harry Kane does," Deane said. "He is not the quickest, but he is intelligent, drops into pockets and allows the team to rotate around him. He has earned the right for the manager to build that structure.

“Dominic Calvert-Lewin is very good at holding the ball up, bringing others into play and competing in the air. Whether he would score the same types of goals as Kane is another question.

Recent findings suggest that “Solanke has the ability, but I am not convinced about his confidence at the moment. The England shirt can weigh heavily.

“Ivan Toney has a strong all-round game, is excellent in the box and is one of the best penalty-takers around. The question would be how he adjusts to the tempo of international football from the league he is playing in.

Recent findings suggest that “Will Lankshear is perhaps a little inexperienced. Bringing him into the squad is one thing; asking him to lead the line ahead of those other players is another.

Industry observers note that “Tuchel might decide not to use a conventional centre-forward. He could put Jude Bellingham or Morgan Rogers further forward and approach it differently. It is very difficult to replicate Kane. He has done amazingly well and is almost irreplaceable.”.

According to data from Transfermarkt, Bellingham has only made one club appearance as an out-and-out centre-forward, compared to 23 for Rogers during his career.

If Deane's prediction comes true and Tuchel does opt for a false-nine approach, the Chelsea man should therefore be at the head of the queue for striking duties, especially having also featured in that role for the Blues already this season against Tottenham Hotspur.

Bellingham has licence to continue in the number 10 role as a result, and Rogers being moved centrally opens the door for a fit-again Bukayo Saka to reclaim his place on the right flank.

However, there is every chance that Kane will recover in time to face Norway, aiming to build on an unparalleled record of 93 goals in 127 matches for his country.

Brian Deane was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of BetWright.

  • The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier remarked Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.

The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.

Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of its 11 directors.

The Upcoming York Times first reported that the 63-year-old Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

Later Thursday, Reuters news agency alleged an intimate relationship between Huang and a second employee, citing unidentified sources.

Industry observers note that those revelations emerged just three days after Huang admitted a relationship with a Chinese woman, whom United States intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The woman, Alice Huang — no relation — is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that runs artificial intelligence (AI) data centers across Southeast Asia and is a major client of Nvidia.

The US government is investigating the startup on suspicion that it secretly sent some of its Nvidia chips to China, violating Washington's curbs on high-end semiconductors.

Those advanced Nvidia processors ‌are ​used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products.

Megaspeed denies the allegations and on Thursday pledged to cooperate with US investigators. Huang, the alleged spy, has been barred from entering Singapore and Taiwan — a key chipmaking island.

While Nvidia's board backed its CEO after the first scandal emerged, market watchers believe the second caused too much reputational damage to one of the world's top three companies by market value.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang doesn't believe in formal succession planning, so with little notice, Nvidia appointed CFO Kress as interim CEO.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Nvidia’s board is working with advisers to identify potential permanent successors.

Sources indicate that kress, other senior Nvidia executives and members of Huang's own family have been mooted as replacements. The family members include his daughter Madison, a senior director of product marketing, and his son Spencer, who presently works in the firm's robotics division.

It has been revealed that rumors also abound over a longer-term solution. On India's CNBC-TV18, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld from the Yale School of Management floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook and ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt.

US President Donald Trump also backed Cook on social media, writing: "A Legend replaces a Legend.".

The scandals have certainly hit Nvidia's market value. Since the first extramarital affair emerged on Sunday, the chipmaker's market capitalization has fallen by well over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion.

Nvidia shares were down more than 9% in premarket trading Thursday, after dropping by 10% earlier this week. Some analysts expect the stock price to struggle in the short term.

Nvidia stock hit all-time highs just a month ago as US technology giants continued to announce billions in spending on AI infrastructure.

Demand for Nvidia's advanced chips is so high, however, that many market analysts expect little impact on near-term sales.

"While Jensen [Huang] is the heart and lungs of the Nvidia story…the organization and its leading-edge GPU technology will go on and [his departure] does not change the entrenched position Nvidia has in the AI Revolution chip arms race," mentioned Dan Ives, a partner, senior managing director and tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, a US-based merchant bank.

Analysts see the biggest long-term risk in strategy and execution. After all, Huang was the leader who picked which ideas Nvidia should bet heavily on and got the whole firm behind them.

His sudden exit is also seen as highly disruptive to the chip designer's strong relationships with AI hyperscalers, Taiwanese chip producer TSMC and foreign governments — especially China.

Huang was Nvidia's main lobbyist on US chip export rules and persuaded US President Donald Trump to ease some curbs on China last year.

Huang is often called a rockstar CEO for his leather jackets instead of suits.

Like Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, he was also seen as a key-person risk as Nvidia’s public image, strategic direction and technical decisions became closely tied to him.

Huang steered the organization for more than three decades and was also respected for his hands-on involvement in product architecture and engineering decisions.

He also insisted on a flat management structure, with around 60 executives reporting directly to him.

Huang has run the company so tightly around his own technical judgment and product decisions that investors may have little sense of how it would function without him.

Sources indicate that at the same time, Nvidia is no longer the startup Huang founded in 1993. The firm has built deep expertise in chip design and software, creating a durable moat that helps protect its huge profits, which topped $120.1 billion last year.

Some analysts argue that its central role in the AI hardware buildout makes it less dependent on Huang’s day-to-day input.

China is promptly playing catch-up with the US in the global race for AI dominance.

While Chinese AI models have lagged behind the likes of ChatGPT and Claude, recent updates from DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot have closed much of the gap on benchmark tests and often beat US rivals on cost and speed.

Beijing is also investing heavily in domestic chips and data centers to reduce reliance on US hardware.

The US has curbed exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips.

However, this move has only slowed the pace of China's AI ambitions.

Reuters reported Thursday that Chinese AI firms are now trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, amid fears the US could further tighten restrictions on advanced chips.

Also Thursday, Beijing accused the US of using the Nvidia spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade" on China.

The problem is likely to dominate talks next week between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen in southern China.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Despite a successful offensive performance and a latest sparkling hat-trick from Pio Esposito, which confirms his rise in power at the forefront of the Nerazzurra attack, Cristian Chivu’s men squandered their lead on the scoreboard three times. A cruel scenario which deeply annoyed the Romanian coach at the microphone of DAZN after the meeting: “we led three times, that’s the regret. #197698. Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
